links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of LLM responses versus sixth-grade health literacy guideline
links.effect: All platforms generated content at high school to college grade reading levels, exceeding recommended sixth-grade health literacy guidelines.
links.quote: All platforms generated content at high school to college grade reading levels, exceeding recommended sixth-grade health literacy guidelines.

links.outcome: Readability of LLM diabetes advice for patients
links.effect: All four LLMs produced high school to college level text, above the recommended sixth-grade level; DeepSeek used more specialized clinical terminology.
links.quote: All platforms generated content at high school to college grade reading levels, exceeding recommended sixth-grade health literacy guidelines.

links.outcome: Differences in LLM responses when patient gender was varied in the prompt
links.effect: DeepSeek exhibited greater gender discrepancy than the other 3 LLMs; the others showed less discrepancy.
links.quote: DeepSeek incorporated more specialized clinical terminology and referenced specific diabetes guidelines not mentioned by ChatGPT, and exhibited greater gender discrepancy than the other 3 LLMs.

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLMs for readability, clinical content, and gender bias using simulated patient prompts without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment intervention.
